classification.difficultyReason: Convert 45 minutes to hours, add the opposite-direction distances and combine that equation with the given speed ratio using routine substitution.

content.prompt:
Solve this problem by introducing two pronumerals and forming a pair of simultaneous equations.

Two aeroplanes pass each other in flight while travelling in opposite directions. Each aeroplane continues on its flight for 45 minutes, after which time the aeroplanes are 840 km apart. The speed of the first aeroplane is $\frac{3}{4}$ of the speed of the other aeroplane. Calculate the average speed of each aeroplane.

answer.short:
First aeroplane: $480\text{ km/h}$; other aeroplane: $640\text{ km/h}$.

Add the distances travelled in $\frac34$ hour and use the speed relationship.
answer.worked:
Let $x$ and $y$ be the average speeds, in km/h, of the first and other aeroplanes respectively. Since $45\text{ minutes}=\frac34\text{ hour}$ and the aeroplanes travel in opposite directions,
$$\begin{align*}
\frac34x+\frac34y&=840 &&\text{(1)}\\
x&=\frac34y &&\text{(2)}
\end{align*}$$
Substitute equation (2) into equation (1):
$$\begin{align*}
\frac34\left(\frac34y\right)+\frac34y&=840\\
\frac{21}{16}y&=840\\
y&=640.
\end{align*}$$
Using equation (2):
$$\begin{align*}
x&=\frac34\times640\\
x&=480.
\end{align*}$$
Check: $\frac34\times480+\frac34\times640=360+480=840$ km, and $480=\frac34\times640$.

The first aeroplane's average speed is $480\text{ km/h}$ and the other aeroplane's average speed is $640\text{ km/h}$.
